text: Seed and planting-material selection (ការជ្រើសរើសពូជ/គ្រាប់ពូជ) should start from the farmer's field conditions, available water, planting season, and intended market -- not simply the variety with the highest advertised yield. Cambodian farmers obtain seed from their own harvest, other farmers, traders, input dealers, cooperatives, extension services, NGOs, or seed companies, using a mix of modern certified seed, modern uncertified seed, and traditional uncertified seed. Preah Vihear farmers should pay particular attention to varieties suited to rain-fed conditions (ពឹងទឹកភ្លៀង) since irrigation access is uneven; a variety requiring reliable irrigation should not be recommended for the dry season simply because it has high yield potential. For small plots, testing a new variety on a small trial area (សាកល្បងពូជ) before planting the whole farm is sensible. Farmers saving their own seed should select from healthy, uniform plants and keep seed dry and protected from insects and moisture. Certified seed may not always be affordable or available -- when farmers use saved or locally purchased seed instead, focus advice on assessing germination, cleanliness, moisture, insect damage, and disease symptoms rather than insisting on certified seed as the only acceptable answer. Do not name a specific rice/cassava/cashew variety as 'the recommended variety for Preah Vihear' without district-level evidence -- Cambodia's national data records many named varieties, but that only confirms they exist somewhere in the country, not that they suit a specific farmer's field, season, and market. Ask the farmer why they're choosing a variety (yield, early maturity, drought resistance, pest resistance, taste, market demand) rather than assuming 'highest yield' is always the goal.
